title: Define and align display rules for "Recent orders" and "Top sellers" blocks on Dashboard and Customer page

environment.name: vcptcore-qa
environment.deploy_verified: schema exposes organizationId/period on both discovery queries; theme artifact pinned to pr-2409

live_seed.purpose: prove the vocabularies are genuinely data-derived, and close the two gaps the static dataset could not cover (a second category, and a status absent from the dictionary)

order.how: real storefront xAPI checkout as the rep under an organization_id-scoped grant: addItem x2 -> addOrUpdateCartShipment (FixedRate/Ground) -> addOrUpdateCartPayment (DefaultManualPaymentMethod) -> createOrderFromCart

lines.product: (146 cm) Atomic Redster S9 Revoshock S 25/26 Skis

order.status_override: AwaitingErpSync, written directly via PUT /api/order/customerOrders to simulate an ERP/3rd-party sync; absent from the Order.Status dictionary

delta.isolation: AcmeCorp / AcmeWest / BuildRight unchanged in both vocabularies - no global recompute

proved: categories are derived from actual sales: chips appeared in a block that previously rendered no chip container at all
the chip is the TOP-LEVEL ancestor resolved via the store catalog outline, not the line item's own deeper categoryId
a status that exists in NO platform dictionary is offered as a chip, labelled with the raw value, and returns its order when applied - the headline claim, unprovable before this seed
cache TTL (SalesRep.Statistics.OrderCacheExpirationMinutes = 1 on this env) did not delay visibility
zero dead chips among the newly created rules, API and UI
live_seed.cleanup_pending: order CO260806-00001 and its AwaitingErpSync status remain on vcptcore-qa and are visible on the rep dashboard; suites 050m/089/091/093 are NOT affected (their assertions are ORG_ACME-scoped and behavioural, never an exact chip-set equality)

Two catalog product images 404 on vcptcore-qa

data_limitations: RESOLVED by the live seed: the category vocabulary is now exercised by 3 categories across 2 scopes, and a genuinely off-dictionary status (AwaitingErpSync) proves the headline claim directly rather than by construction.

Root cause of the original thinness identified: the pre-existing seeded orders carry a null OrderLineItem.CategoryId, while an order placed through the real storefront checkout carries it correctly. This is a gap in the order seeder, not a product defect - worth fixing so the category filter has standing coverage.
